name: James Allison
description: James Allison shared the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that blocking the immune checkpoint protein CTLA-4 unleashes T cells to attack tumors, founding the field of immune checkpoint therapy. His foundational mouse experiments in the 1990s at UC Berkeley demonstrated that anti-CTLA-4 antibodies could eradicate established tumors, a concept that eventually became the drug ipilimumab (Yervoy), the first checkpoint inhibitor approved by the FDA. Allison chairs the Department of Immunology at MD Anderson and his Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy collaborations have catalyzed combination checkpoint blockade trials now standard of care for melanoma, lung, and bladder cancers. He holds numerous industry advisory roles and his basic-science discoveries have generated billions of dollars in therapeutic value. Allison is also an accomplished harmonica player and has performed with Willie Nelson.
